title: Matched Reef Check surveys showed small mean depth contrasts in coral bleaching at 0-30 m in 1998-2019
abstract: We compared coral bleaching at two depths in the same site and on the same date. The sample has 1,683 Reef Check pairs at 984 sites in 49 countries from 1998 to 2019. Depths were 0-30 m and differed by at least 3 m. Each site had equal weight. The mean deep minus shallow contrast was -0.287 percentage points. Its 95% country bootstrap interval was -0.710 to +0.185. The Pacific mean was negative, but the signs differed across oceans. Both period means were negative and both intervals included zero. Only 96 pairs had CoRTAD TSA_DHW of at least 4; their interval was wide. Matching removes differences in site, date, and data source. It does not remove differences in coral communities or survey detection with depth. Most pairs had no bleaching at either depth. The result applies to these selected surveys. It does not establish a causal depth refuge, a climate trend, or an air pollution effect. The package gives code, paired data, source hashes, an independent numerical check, and a figure.

display.caption: Deep minus shallow bleaching. Each site has equal weight. Bars show 95% intervals from a country bootstrap. The sample has depths of 0-30 m and a depth gap of at least 3 m.

A prior campaign study tested heat dose using repeat-site and month controls in the same raw data. We test a different contrast: depth within site and date. Observations overlap, so this is not independent data replication.
